blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: Isaiah 40-55 announces comfort and return from Babylon through creation and exodus imagery, presenting a new homecoming without implying that displacement trauma or postreturn conflict simply vanished. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. The evidence leaves some details unresolved.

A literary feature to notice is that The Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete sixty-six-chapter witness broadly aligned with the Masoretic tradition but containing thousands of orthographic and substantive differences; other Qumran Isaiah manuscripts and pesharim show active transmission and interpretation. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. A more precise reconstruction remains disputed.
